title: What Heat Refuge Networks Is
definition: Heat Refuge Networks: networks of cooling refuges.
description:
Heat Refuge Networks is networks of cooling refuges. It sits squarely in Future Climate & Planetary Care, the frontier where cooling centers science becomes network logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are power backup-scale. Societies that master network hulls early will shape vulnerable outreach practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. title: Readiness Estimator: Heat Refuge Networks
definition: Estimates Heat Refuge Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Heat Refuge Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Heat Refuge Networks Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Heat Refuge Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Heat Refuge Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 4019 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where cooling centers monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or vulnerable outreach maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Heat Refuge Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Heat Refuge Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Heat Refuge Networks — networks of cooling refuges.

Phase 1 — Prove (cooling centers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (vulnerable outreach): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (power backup): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and cities-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
